data.name: Fetch™
data.detailed_description:
How far would you go to save your best friend?

The core of Fetch is the sensational and fantastic journey of a boy attempting to rescue for his best friend: his dog, Bear. It is a romp through the marvel of childhood, equal parts adventure and arcade. Fetch replaces the traditional brain-bending puzzles of the adventure game genre with high quality arcade experiences.

- 50 in-game and Steam Achievements
- Built in Strategy Guide
- Concept Art
- Re-playable Arcade mini-games

Originally released only to iPhone/iPad, now coming to PC/Mac and Android devices.

We are grateful to all the loyal fans who pushed for the port to other devices. We love the game, and hope you do too.

reviews.review:
Developed by Big Fish Studios and published by BFG Entertainment, Fetch is a family-oriented adventure that combines an engaging story with light arcade gameplay to deliver an experience that is both entertaining and emotionally satisfying. Instead of focusing solely on traditional point-and-click mechanics, the game introduces a refreshing blend of exploration, mini-games, and cinematic storytelling that makes it accessible to players of all ages. Its charming presentation and heartfelt narrative emphasize imagination, determination, and the enduring connection between a child and his loyal companion, creating an adventure that feels welcoming from beginning to end.

The story centers on Milo, a young boy whose beloved dog, Bear, mysteriously vanishes after an unexpected encounter. Refusing to give up on his faithful friend, Milo embarks on an imaginative journey through unusual locations filled with hidden dangers, curious characters, and magical surprises. While the premise is simple, it is supported by a sincere emotional core that encourages players to keep moving forward. The narrative gradually unfolds through exploration and environmental storytelling, maintaining a sense of wonder without relying on complicated plot twists. Its straightforward approach allows the friendship between Milo and Bear to remain the emotional heart of the adventure.

Gameplay strikes a balance between casual accessibility and engaging variety. Exploration follows familiar adventure game conventions as players search environments, interact with objects, and uncover clues that lead to new areas. Instead of presenting difficult inventory puzzles that may frustrate newcomers, Fetch emphasizes arcade-inspired mini-games that test reflexes, timing, and coordination. These sequences provide a welcome change of pace and keep the gameplay feeling energetic throughout the journey. The inclusion of an in-game strategy guide also ensures that players can overcome obstacles without becoming stuck, making the experience especially suitable for younger audiences and those who simply want to enjoy the story.

The visual presentation is one of the game's greatest strengths. Every environment is filled with bright colors, imaginative scenery, and detailed artwork that captures the sense of adventure seen through a child's eyes. Character animations are expressive, helping communicate emotion even during quieter moments, while the varied settings keep exploration consistently enjoyable. Rather than pursuing realistic graphics, the developers chose a stylized art direction that gives the game a timeless quality, allowing its environments to remain attractive years after release.

Audio design complements the visuals effectively. The soundtrack shifts naturally between playful, mysterious, and emotional moments, reinforcing the mood of each scene without becoming repetitive. Sound effects add life to the world and enhance the arcade segments, while the restrained use of dialogue allows the game's atmosphere and music to carry much of the emotional storytelling. Together, the audiovisual presentation creates an inviting experience that appeals to both children and adults.

Fetch also offers additional content that extends its value beyond the main adventure. Steam achievements encourage completionists to fully explore every aspect of the game, while replayable mini-games provide opportunities to revisit favorite challenges. Unlockable concept artwork offers an interesting glimpse into the game's artistic development, rewarding players who enjoy exploring everything the adventure has to offer. These extras may not dramatically increase the game's length, but they provide worthwhile incentives for those who appreciate collecting bonuses and revisiting completed content.

Despite its many strengths, the game is not without shortcomings. Players who prefer complex adventure titles with demanding puzzles may find the simplified gameplay lacking in depth. Some mini-games become repetitive over time, and the overall campaign can be completed in a relatively short number of hours. The story is heartfelt but predictable, favoring accessibility over narrative complexity. However, these limitations stem from deliberate design choices rather than poor execution, as the game clearly prioritizes a broad audience and a relaxed pace instead of presenting an intense challenge.

Overall, Fetch succeeds by delivering a warm, imaginative, and family-friendly adventure that balances exploration, arcade action, and heartfelt storytelling. Its charming visuals, enjoyable gameplay variety, approachable mechanics, and emotional focus make it an easy recommendation for casual players, families, and anyone seeking a lighthearted adventure with genuine charm. Although seasoned adventure fans may wish for greater puzzle complexity and a longer campaign, the game remains a polished and memorable experience that captures the joy of friendship and childhood imagination.

Rating: 8/10
